title: geo-score watch run
description: One saved run: every question asked to every engine, what each answer cited, and what it cost. The summary is derived from the samples and can be recomputed.

channel.description: Answers came from the providers' APIs, not the consumer apps.

target_url.description: The page this question tracks, or empty. Since 1.6.0 saved as resolved: an absolute http(s) URL as written (fragment and utm_* parameters dropped), or a path starting with / joined to https:// and the brand's first domain; any other value is saved empty. Older runs hold the value as written, and reports resolve it the same way.

branded.description: The optional branded column of the question file. yes or no decides whether the question counts as naming the brand; auto (the default) follows brand_in_query.

brand_in_query.description: The question names the brand, an alias or a brand domain, by the matcher used on answers (whole words for Latin script, anywhere for Chinese, Japanese and Korean). Set at run time; for runs saved without it, reports compute it from the question text and the run's brand.

competitor_in_query.description: The question names a tracked competitor.

recorded.description: What this run records on each answer when the provider gives it: spans (where the answer's citations sit, and supported_share) and sources (sources_listed and sources_used). A run saved before these were recorded has no such list, and a report then says these were not recorded rather than that the engines gave none. Ignored by pooling and diff.

questions_hash.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the JSON array of [query_id, text] pairs, sorted, written with no spaces and with non-ASCII characters as \u escapes; the text is case-folded, its whitespace collapsed to single spaces and stripped. Two runs that asked the same questions share it, whatever their order. Saved since 1.6.0; for older runs it can be computed from queries.

summary.description: Derived from the samples. Runs saved before the clustered intervals and the branded split lack those fields; reports recompute the summary for them.

headline.description: The headline rate: answers to questions that do not name the brand. Equal to overall when no question names it.

branded.description: Answers to questions that name the brand, with their question_ids. Kept out of the headline.

brand_flags.description: run: brand_in_query was set when the run was made. computed: the run predates the flag and it was found from the saved question text when the summary was made.

with_citations.description: Answers from this engine that carry at least one citation, of any domain. Added in 1.6.0; reports recompute the summary of a run saved without it. When the engine answered 5 or more questions and none of its answers cites, the report warns that the API's answer format may have changed; it counts questions, not answers, because the answers to one question move together.

with_searches.description: Answers from this engine that expose at least one search query. Added in 1.6.0.

searched_without_queries.description: Answers from this engine (OpenAI, Gemini or Anthropic) whose usage reports at least one search call but which expose no search query, as when an OpenAI-compatible base_url returns web_search_call items with no action. Reports recompute the summary of a run saved without it.

named_first.description: Answers from this engine whose mention_order for the brand is 1: it is named before every other brand in the config. Added in 1.6.0; reports recompute the summary of a run saved without it.

any_named.description: Answers from this engine that name at least one brand in the config, yours included: the n of named_first. Added in 1.6.0.

mention_share.description: The mean of the brand's mention_share over this engine's answers that name it; null when none does. Added in 1.6.0.

named_first.description: Answers that name this brand before every other brand in the config (mention_order 1). Added in 1.6.0; reports recompute the summary of a run saved without it.

any_named.description: Answers that name at least one brand in the config: the n of named_first, the same in every row. Added in 1.6.0.

mention_share.description: The mean of this brand's mention_share over the answers that name it; null when none does. Added in 1.6.0.

by_question.description: One entry per question, in question order: who the answers cite and name, as counts. Added in 1.6.0; reports recompute the summary of a run saved without it.

tracked_pages.description: One entry per page named in target_url, questions that share a page together, in question order; empty when no question tracks a page. Added in 1.6.0 and read from the saved citations; reports recompute the summary of a run saved without it.

searches.description: What the engines searched for, read from the search queries the answers (status ok) expose. Counts that describe the searches, not a judgement of them.

answers_exposing.description: Answers that expose at least one search query.

top.description: The 15 most frequent search queries, lower-cased with whitespace collapsed, with how often each was run.

answers_searched_without_queries.description: Answers from OpenAI, Gemini or Anthropic engines whose usage reports at least one search call but which expose no search query: the engine searched and the endpoint did not return what it searched for, as an OpenAI-compatible base_url may do. Perplexity and OpenRouter answers are never counted, because their adapters record one search per answer whatever happened. Reports recompute the summary of a run saved without it.

modifiers.description: Over every exposed search query (each answer's queries, de-duplicated within the answer): how many contain a year and how many a ranking or comparison word. A query counts once for each, however many it holds. A query that repeats the question's own words counts too. Reports recompute the summary of a run saved without it.

with_year.description: Queries holding a four-digit number from 1900 to 2099 with no letter, digit or underscore on either side (a Chinese, Japanese or Korean character beside it is a break, so 2026年 counts).

with_ranking_word.description: Queries holding best, top, vs, versus, review, reviews, compare, comparison, alternative or alternatives as a whole word, any letter case, or 最好, 最佳, 推荐, 排行, 排名, 哪家, 哪个好, 对比 or 评测 anywhere.

rate.description: A citation rate. Blocks from runs saved by 1.2.0 carry only the Wilson interval.

cited_ci.description: 95% Wilson interval, every answer counted as independent.

cited_ci_clustered.description: 95% interval from a bootstrap over questions (2,000 resamples, seeded from the run id), never narrower than cited_ci. The one to quote when answered > n_questions.

diff.description: What `watch diff --format json` prints (and the MCP diff tool with format json). Not stored in run files.

alpha.description: Threshold on p_adjusted for a change.

min_questions.description: Fewer questions answered in both runs than this gives the verdict 'too few questions to tell'.

pooled.description: Since 1.6.0. What `watch report --since DAYS` or `watch report --runs A..B` prints with --format json (and the MCP report tool with since): several saved runs counted as one set of answers. Every run pooled asked the same questions (the same questions_hash) as many times each (the same runs, so every run weighs the same) on the same engines with the same providers and models, from the same country, with the same brand domains and URL prefixes as the newest; otherwise the command refuses and names the runs that differ. Not stored in run files.

channel.description: Answers came from the providers' APIs, not the consumer apps.

planned.description: Samples in the run: questions x engines x asks.

since_days.description: The --since window in days: runs started that many days before the report or later. Null with --runs.

from.description: started_at of the first run pooled.

to.description: started_at of the newest run pooled.

days.description: Calendar days (UTC) from the first run's start to the newest run's, both counted.

questions_hash.description: The questions_hash every run pooled shares.

overall.description: Every answer of every run pooled, with planned, errors and skipped as in summary.overall.

headline.description: Answers to questions that do not name the brand, as in summary.headline. cited_ci_clustered resamples questions, each with all its answers from every run and engine: the interval to quote.

branded.description: Answers to questions that name the brand, flagged as in the newest run, with their question_ids.

brand_flags.description: As in summary.brand_flags, for the newest run.

engines.description: One row per engine measured, every run's answers from it pooled, its interval resampling questions.

notes.description: The API-channel note, what pooling does and does not show, the run report's notes on questions that name the brand, on what counts as not measured and on what a citation rate does not predict, and any note on how questions were flagged.

before.description: Share of answers citing the brand in the earlier run, every answer counted (unpaired).

p_value.description: Unpaired two-proportion z-test, as in 1.2.0. Kept for compatibility; the verdict does not use it.

n_pairs.description: Question x engine pairs answered in both runs.

n_asks.description: Answers per run that enter the paired comparison: for each pair, the asks both runs made.

before_paired.description: Share of those answers citing the brand in the earlier run.

delta_ci.description: 95% interval for delta_pp, in points: a paired bootstrap over questions, never narrower than Newcombe's interval. Null below min_questions.

p_paired.description: Exact two-sided paired test: McNemar when each question has one answer per run, otherwise the exact sign-flip test on each question's net change in cited answers (McNemar's test with each question's answers kept together).

p_adjusted.description: p_paired after Holm's correction across the engine rows and the overall row.

warning.description: Engine rows only, since 1.6.0. Present when the share of this engine's answers carrying any citation fell from at least 50% to below 5% with the same model, and the later run answered at least 5 questions on this engine. An adapter reads one answer format, so a provider that changed its format reads as an engine that stopped citing. The verdict is left as computed; the same words are in the diff's notes.

by_question.description: One question's answers, counted. Every number is a count of answers (status ok) over every engine and ask, never a rate.

branded.description: The question counts as naming the brand, as in summary.branded.

none_named.description: Answers whose text names neither the brand nor any tracked competitor. They may name brands the config does not list.

searched.description: Whether the engine searched the web for each answer, from what the run saved: yes when it reported a search, exposed a search query or cited a URL; no when an OpenAI, Gemini or Anthropic answer shows none of these; unknown for Perplexity and OpenRouter, whose APIs search on every call or do not say.

leader.description: The tracked brand (yours or a competitor) cited by the most answers, when the question has at least 4 answers and that count is above zero and above every other tracked brand's. Otherwise null.

tracked_page.description: The answers to the questions that track one page. A cited URL is that page when the two are equal once www, letter case, a trailing slash, the query string, the fragment and percent-encoding are set aside; another path or locale is another page. Every number is a count of answers (status ok).

target_url.description: The page, resolved as in queries[].target_url.

other_own_cited.description: Answers that do not cite the page but cite another URL the brand owns. A citation left as an unresolved redirect counts as neither.

top_other_url.description: Among those answers, the brand's URL cited by the most of them, exactly as cited (ties go to the first in sort order); null when there are none.

mention_order.description: Since 1.6.0. Where the answer first names this brand among the brands in the config (the brand and every competitor): 1 when it is named before all the others it names, 2 when one is named before it, and so on. The offset of a brand is that of the earliest match of its name, aliases or domains, with the matcher of mentioned. Null when the answer does not name it, and for brands first named at the same offset, as when one name is inside another. Read from the answer as saved (its first 20,000 characters), so brands the config does not list are never counted.

mention_share.description: Since 1.6.0. The share of the answer's sentences that name this brand, every sentence counted the same. A sentence ends at a line break, at 。！？, or at . ! ? followed by whitespace or the end of the text; a piece with no letter or digit is not a sentence. Null when the answer does not name it. Read from the answer as saved (its first 20,000 characters).

citation.description: A source as citations records one: the URL cleaned (fragment and utm_* parameters dropped, a Gemini redirect followed where the exact page matters), the domain that decides who owns it, and the title (at most 200 characters).

span.description: Where one citation sits in the answer as saved: character offsets, start included, end left out, cut to the saved answer's first 20,000 characters.

urls.description: The sources the provider ties to this place, read as citations reads them (at most 20). The domain that decides who owns one is the one citations or sources_listed records for it, or its host.

kind.description: segment: the provider gives the text a source supports (Gemini's url_citation annotations and grounding supports, Claude's text blocks with citations). marker: the provider gives where the citation sits (OpenAI's and OpenRouter's url_citation annotations, Perplexity's [n] markers); the text it supports is the sentence it closes, and the marker itself is not counted as text.

supported_share.description: The share of the answer (as saved) supported by a span with a URL the brand owns. Sentences are mention_share's, split with every marker blanked out. |s| is a sentence's non-whitespace characters, markers left out; c(s) is the part of them the brand's spans support: all of |s| when a marker credits s (a marker credits the sentence it sits in when text precedes it there, else the sentence before), else the characters of s inside the brand's segments. See guide/watch-methodology.md, section 9.

chars.description: The sum of c(s) over the sum of |s|, over every sentence.

sentences.description: Sentences with c(s) > 0 over all sentences.

weighted.description: The position-adjusted share of arXiv 2311.09735, section 2.2.1, Eq. 3, counted in characters: the sum over sentences of c(s) x exp(-pos(s) / |S|) over the sum of |s|; pos(s) is a sentence's index from 0, |S| the number of sentences. A sentence several sources support counts in full, where the paper shares it among them.

support_summary.description: One engine's answer share, beside its cited rate and never merged into it, over its answers (status ok) whose supported_share is measured. Reports recompute the summary of a run saved without it; answers saved without spans are not measured.

answers.description: Answers measured. 0: not measured, and the medians are null.

above_zero.description: Answers measured whose supported_share.chars is above zero.

sources_summary.description: One engine's sources listed and used, over its answers (status ok) that record sources_listed and sources_used. Reports recompute the summary of a run saved without it.

listed.description: Sources listed, summed over those answers.

used.description: Sources used, summed over those answers.

used_rate.description: used / listed; null when nothing was listed.

you_listed.description: Answers that list a URL the brand owns.

you_used.description: Answers whose text uses a URL the brand owns.

consistency_summary.description: One engine's repeat consistency in one run: for each question it answered more than once with answers that cite, the mean Jaccard overlap of the cited domains between every two of those answers; descriptive only, never part of the cited rate and not read by diff. Answers that cite nothing are left out. Added in 1.8.0; reports recompute the summary of a run saved without it.

questions.description: Questions with two or more answers that cite. 0: not measured (each question asked once, or too few answers that cite).

answers.description: Answers that cite, summed over those questions.

median.description: The median over those questions of each question's mean Jaccard; null when no question is measured.

lowest.description: Up to 3 questions whose answers did not all cite the same domains, lowest first.

cited.description: Answers citing a URL this brand owns.
The answer cites a URL the brand owns.

rank.description: Position of the brand among the distinct domains the answer cites.

mentioned.description: The answer text names the brand, an alias or its domain.

search_queries.description: What the engine searched for, when the provider exposes it.

target_cited.description: Since 1.6.0. The answer cites the page the question tracks (target_url), matched as in $defs/tracked_page; null when the question tracks no page.

other_own_cited.description: Since 1.6.0. The answer does not cite the tracked page but cites another URL the brand owns; null when the question tracks no page.

spans.description: Where the answer's citations sit, in the order the provider gave them (at most 500). Present only when every citation came with a position the provider documents. Absent: not measured, never an empty answer share. That is the case for an answer with no citation, one with a citation the provider gave no usable position for (an endpoint that drops annotations looks the same), a Perplexity answer whose search results carry no id (the number its documentation maps a [n] mark to), one over a cap, and every answer of a run that predates the field.

sources_listed.description: Every source the API returned beside the answer (at most 100), for APIs that list sources apart from the ones the text marks: Perplexity (search_results, or the older citations list, when the text has [n] marks and no result's id disagrees with its place in the list) and Gemini with api generate_content (groundingChunks, when it returns grounding supports). Absent: not measured. citations, and so cited, is unchanged by it.

sources_used.description: Present with sources_listed: the listed sources the answer's text marks (Perplexity's [n] marks, the n-th listed source for [n], as citations has always read them; Gemini's grounding supports).
